applies_why: The judge text counts Matthew 1:18 and 1:25 from the cited-in line D2 as witnesses that break challenger link C3, which is exactly the counting that K-G4 governs.
quote: CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN -- [L1] Matthew 1:18 'before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost' and Matthew 1:25 'knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son' contradict C3's claim of espousal union
rule_words: A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count.
room: 'counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round' -- reading A: the rule governs only a separate witness tally and is satisfied by the judge quoting the verse text itself; reading B: letting a cited verse count against a link requires the judge to quote the earlier round's pressing sentence and name that round; I weighed A against B and adopted B, because 'the earlier round' means a debate round, and this text quotes scripture only and names no round.
why: The judge let Matthew 1:18 and 1:25 (and Luke 1:34) count toward breaking C3 while quoting only scripture and naming no round, leaving undone what K-G4 requires before a cited verse may count as a witness.
